latest_release.name: v4.7.0
latest_release.body: > v4.7.0 is the next minor release. ## 📣 Some news ### 🧪 Try Nitro v3 today You can now build your Nuxt 4 app with [Nitro v3](https://nitro.build) ([#37101](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/37101)). Nitro v3 is what Nuxt 5 is built on, so this is a way to move your server code (and your modules) over before you upgrade Nuxt itself. There's no config to change. Just add `nitro` to your dependencies: ```bash npm install nitro ``` If `nitro` is in your `package.json`, Nuxt builds with Nitro v3. To go back, just remove it. > [!CAUTION] > This is **highly experimental**. Nitro v3 is still a release candidate, and there are no guarantees. Please try it on a branch, not in production. 🙏 Do give Nitro v3 a try! On our benchmark app with about 170 pages, the same app on 4.7 served 33% more requests per second on its home page with Nitro v3 than with Nitro v2 (926 to 1,236), and 44% more on a page with 1,000 links (219 to 316), with identical HTML. On Nuxt 4, Nitro v3 runs with a compatibility layer, `nitroLegacy`, which keeps imports from `h3`, `nitropack` and `#imports` resolving, keeps the Nitro v2 auto-imports, `useRuntimeConfig(event)`, `event.node` and the Nitro v2 hooks working, and keeps a long list of h3 v1 behaviours. Once things work, set `nitroLegacy: false` to find the code that still depends on it. A few things change with Nitro v3 regardless. The main one is route rules: `/blog/*` now also applies to `/blog/2026/hello`. Nuxt warns about each rule whose meaning changes (`NUXT_B4029`), and stops on a rule with more than one wildcard, like `/api/*/items/**`, which you can rewrite with a named parameter (`/api/:id/items/**`). Your app matches route rules the same way as the server, so Nuxt-only rules like `appMiddleware` and `ssr` apply to the same paths on both. The other is imports. If your server code imported a package your app didn't depend on, Nitro v2 fell back to Nuxt's own dependencies. Nitro v3 doesn't, so `nuxt dev` fails with something like `Cannot find package 'ufo'`. Make sure every package your server code imports is in your `package.json`. The upgrade guide has [the full list](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/getting-started/upgrade#testing-nitro-v3). If something breaks for you (and it might), please [open an issue](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/new/choose) and mention Nitro v3. ❤️ ### 🖥️ Nuxt CLI 4.1 Nuxt 4.7 also comes with [Nuxt CLI 4.1](https://github.com/nuxt/cli/releases/tag/v4.1.0). The most visible change is that the CLI now renders the whole production build itself, from a set of new build hooks, with every builder and server builder (thanks to [@atinux](https://github.com/atinux), [nuxt/cli#1662](https://github.com/nuxt/cli/pull/1662), [#37194](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/37194)): `nuxt generate` shows the prerendered routes in the same way, and ends by suggesting where to deploy. Logs from Nuxt and modules stay inside the build output rather than breaking out of it ([nuxt/cli#1705](https://github.com/nuxt/cli/pull/1705)), and with [nitropack v2.14](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro-v2/releases/tag/v2.14.0) a route that fails to prerender is listed with the pages that link to it ([#37245](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/37245)). There's more: - `nuxt dev --https` serves over HTTP/2 (thanks to [@ProgramRipper](https://github.com/ProgramRipper), [nuxt/cli#1694](https://github.com/nuxt/cli/pull/1694)) - you can click and scroll inside the panes of the dev panel (thanks to [@Flo0806](https://github.com/Flo0806), [nuxt/cli#1665](https://github.com/nuxt/cli/pull/1665)) - copying a URL or an error works without a system clipboard, for example over SSH or

detail.readme:
# Nuxt

Nuxt is a free and open-source framework with an intuitive and extendable way to create type-safe, performant and production-grade full-stack web applications and websites with Vue.js. It provides a number of features that make it easy to build fast, SEO-friendly, and scalable web applications, including: - Server-side rendering, static site generation, hybrid rendering and edge-side rendering - Automatic routing with code-splitting and pre-fetching - Data fetching and state management - Search engine optimization and defining meta tags - Auto imports of components, composables and utils - TypeScript with zero configuration - Go full-stack with our server/ directory - Extensible with [300+ modules](https://nuxt.com/modules) - Deployment to a variety of [hosting platforms](https://nuxt.com/deploy) - ...[and much more](https://nuxt.com) 🚀 ## 🚀 Getting Started Use the following command to create a new starter project. This will create a starter project with all the necessary files and dependencies: ```bash npm create nuxt@latest ``` > [!TIP] > Discover also [nuxt.new](https://nuxt.new): Open a Nuxt starter on CodeSandbox, StackBlitz or locally to get up and running in a few seconds. ## 💻 Vue Development Simple, intuitive and powerful, Nuxt lets you write Vue components in a way that makes sense. Every repetitive task is automated, so you can focus on writing your full-stack Vue application with confidence. Example of an `app.vue`: ```vue ``` ## 📖 Documentation We highly recommend you take a look at the [Nuxt documentation](https://nuxt.com/docs) to level up. It’s a great resource for learning more about the framework. It covers everything from getting started to advanced topics. ## 🧩 Modules Discover our [list of modules](https://nuxt.com/modules) to supercharge your Nuxt project, created by the Nuxt team and community. ## ❤️ Contribute We invite you to contribute and help improve Nuxt 💚 Here are a few ways you can get involved: - **Reporting Bugs:** If you come across any bugs or issues, please check out the [reporting bugs guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/community/reporting-bugs) to learn how to submit a bug report. - **Suggestions:** Have ideas to enhance Nuxt? We'd love to hear them! Check out the [contribution guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/community/contribution) to share your suggestions. - **Questions:** If you have questions or need assistance, the [getting help guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/community/getting-help) provides resources to help you out. ## 🏠 Local Development Follow the docs to [Set Up Your Local Development Environment](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/community/framework-contribution#setup) to contribute to the framework and documentation. ## 🛟 Professional Support - Technical audit & consulting: [Nuxt Experts](https://nuxt.com/enterprise/support) - Custom development & more: [Nuxt Agencies Partners](https://nuxt.com/enterprise/agencies) ## 🔗 Follow Us
